description: Team Tharsis is six students brought together by a sharded passion for space. We met at different space events. With our skills in coding, CAD, critical thinking, design and research, we use our different perspectives and skills to collaborate and solve problems.
summary:
CONSENT NOTE: all members of the team have consented to images & voices of them being used in the project proof is attached below in the "Other" data section. Our project focuses on making navigation on Mars easier and safer for astronauts. We developed an interactive map of Mars that could eventually be integrated into an astronaut's helmet. Our team split up the work based on our different skills. Our researchers used NASA resources to gather information about Mars and the Tharsis region, while our software developers built the mapping system with the help of SI tools. We also had a CAD designer create a 3D model of the Tharsis Plateau using Tinkercad, and a concept artist sketch the PHOTON-VI helmet. The helmet concept is designed to display useful information such as altitude, possible terrain hazards, distance to a destination and estimated travel time.

Throughout the project, we used SI to help with research, coding, fixing errors and improving our software. It also helped us work with NASA datasets, calculate routes and resources, design the HUD interface and test different features. We used SI for some documentation and video editing as well. All images used were real and not SI-generated, and the original NASA data was not altered. PHOTON-VI is still a concept, so our simulations are possible missions rather than real astronaut experiences.

*IMPORTANT NOTE: To explore our project, download the ZIP file, extract its contents and open the HTML file in a web browser.*
